title: A shared place is a map on the desktop
summary: On the desktop a place someone shares is a small map with a marker that opens on OpenStreetMap, no longer a line of letters and numbers, and quotes, the chat list and notifications call it a location. On the iPhone a shared place is where you are, with a pin on its map. The desktop gets 0.2.77 and the iPhone TestFlight build 143017 (1.4.34); Android stays at 0.2.75.

changes.title: Desktop: a shared place is a map
changes.description: A place shared from a phone showed on the desktop as the text khandaq-location: and its coordinates. It is now a map card: the map around the place with a marker on it, and under it Location and the coordinates; a click opens the place on openstreetmap.org. The map comes from OpenStreetMap through the proxy set in the app's settings, without cookies; while it loads, or when it cannot, the card keeps its place and tries again after a minute.

changes.title: Desktop: a place is called a location everywhere
changes.description: A reply to a place, the reply bar, search, export and the queue of unsent messages show Location and the coordinates; the chat list, notifications and in-app bands say Location, and a reaction to a place says it was to your location.

changes.title: iPhone: a shared place is where you are
changes.description: A place shared from the iPhone could be kilometres off, because the app asked for the reduced accuracy. It now waits up to 8 seconds for a fresh fix and sends the most accurate one; with Precise Location off for the app, it asks once for the exact place, and a share that gets no fix says so. The map in the chat has a pin on the place, with the coordinates as its caption; quotes, the chat list and notifications say Location, and holding a chat in the list shows its places, photos, videos and quotes as the chat does.
